rules.concern: A valid signature establishes attestation, not authority.
Authorization requires valid key, recognized issuer, authority derivation, scope coverage, and valid state in addition to signature validity.
Commitments use RFC8785 canonical bytes with a registered ASCII domain, NUL separator, and SHA-256.
Commitment text is exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters with no prefix or surrounding whitespace.
Artifact domains come only from the closed protocol registry and unknown domains fail closed.
Verifier derives expected domain from artifact type; artifact-supplied domain cannot choose the commitment domain.
Signature input is reconstructed from the closed-schema unsigned envelope and the signature member is excluded from signed bytes.
Ed25519 signatures and future public keys use strict unpadded RFC4648 base64url with decode/reencode canonicality and exact decoded lengths.
Signed artifact type and signed artifact domain must match the closed registry.

Raw security artifacts pass resource limits, strict UTF-8, tokenization, duplicate-name detection, lexical profile, I-JSON, schema, semantic validation, canonicalization, commitment, signature, key, authority, and protocol validation in order.
Duplicate property names are detected before map/object conversion and escaped names compare after escape processing.
BOM, comments, trailing commas, NaN, infinities, invalid UTF-8, lone surrogates, multiple top-level values, unsupported extensions, and leading/trailing whitespace are rejected.
Canonicalization performs no Unicode normalization, folding, transliteration, or homoglyph replacement.
Property ordering follows RFC8785 UTF-16 code-unit ordering and invalid Unicode fails closed.
Security-critical JSON numeric tokens are nonnegative decimal integers in 0..2^53-1 with no sign, decimal, exponent, or forbidden leading zero.
Numeric restrictions are enforced against original lexical tokens before host-language numeric conversion and recursively in extensions.
Signed timestamps use exactly YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ, UTC only, no fractional seconds, valid calendar values, and no leap second 60.
Wall-clock timestamps do not implicitly establish transaction ordering; deterministic ordering uses logical epoch or another committed logical sequence.
Every signed security-relevant artifact carries the mandatory protocol header and empty extension containers in ESRM v0.1.
Unknown critical extensions fail deterministically and security meaning cannot enter through uncommitted extension material.
Reconciliation result algebra is exactly MATCH, DIVERGED, INSUFFICIENT, and UNRESOLVED with mutually exclusive meanings.
Timeout does not imply divergence; open-window uncertainty is INSUFFICIENT and closed-window unresolved uncertainty is UNRESOLVED.
Later evidence creates a new reconciliation artifact or epoch rather than mutating an earlier conclusion.
Absence of observed evidence is not evidence of absence unless authoritative closed-world coverage over the relevant domain and interval is proven and committed.
Authority consumption is append-only and irreversible; later proof of rejection, non-effect, crash, or timeout cannot restore the consumed authority.
A legitimate later attempt after consumption requires a distinct newly derived authority; proof of non-occurrence may justify regrant but never reuse.
Authority consumption is not equivalent to external effect; durable consumption and CROSSING_POSSIBLE records precede any externally visible effect-capable dispatch.
After CROSSING_POSSIBLE without conclusive external evidence, effect status is UNKNOWN and cannot be converted to success, failure, or reusable authority.
Dispatch intent is an immutable, domain-committed artifact establishing prepared authorized attempt only, not transmission, execution, observation, or settlement.
Boundary-crossing artifact proves only that the protected effect boundary could be crossed; it does not prove transport or effect.
Target recovery capability cannot be established by adapter self-declaration; it requires committed capability evidence.
Durable idempotency evidence must establish same effect identity plus same canonical payload implies at most one semantic effect.
Recovery observes occurred effects, starts a new transition after proven non-occurrence, retransmits the same effect only with verified durable idempotency, otherwise remains unresolved.

Retransmission under durable idempotency preserves effect identity, canonical operation commitment, target, and semantic transition; any security-relevant change creates a new transition requiring new authority.
Transport attempts and semantic effects are distinct; multiple attempts belong to one transition only with verified durable deduplication.
Transport acknowledgement and executor response are not independent proof of semantic effect or empirical observation.
ESRM v0.1 does not claim universal exactly-once execution.
Unknown external effect status never becomes false success, false failure, or restored execution authority.
Cryptographic validity, authority validity, and empirical validity remain distinct; speculative, empirical, and adjudicated epistemic roles remain distinct.
Settlement requires independently distinguishable committed facts for state, derivation, authority, admission, consumption, dispatch, observation, reconciliation, and settlement.
